title: Common-denominator conjecture for multivariate characteristic functions
statement:
Let $n$ and $m$ be nonnegative integers, let $t_1,
obreak\ldots,t_{n+m}$ be parameters, and let $\chi_{n,m}^{(t_1,\ldots,t_{n+m})}(x_1,\ldots,x_{n+m}\mid\rho,q)$ be the multivariate characteristic functions defined by the generating series in the paper, with $|\rho|,|q|<1$. Let $w_{n+m}(x_1,\ldots,x_{n+m}\mid\rho)$ be the functions defined by the stated iterative relationship, and set

$$
W_{n,m}(x_1,\ldots,x_{n+m}\mid\rho,q)=\prod_{i=0}^{\infty}w_{n+m}(x_1,\ldots,x_{n+m}\mid\rho q^i).
$$

**Common-denominator conjecture.** For all $n,m,t_1,\ldots,t_{n+m}$, the functions $\chi_{n,m}^{(t_1,\ldots,t_{n+m})}(x_1,\ldots,x_{n+m}\mid\rho,q)$ are rational functions having the common denominator $W_{n,m}(x_1,\ldots,x_{n+m}\mid\rho,q)$.

The conjecture extends known bivariate characteristic-function identities to more variables; the paper notes that no results concerning more variables were then available. Its status is not established in the supplied text.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.00316

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2017).
source_name: Paweł J. Szabłowski, “Multivariate generating functions built of Chebyshev polynomials and some of its applications and generalizations”, arXiv:1706.00316 (2021).
